topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the conceptual framework of the hallmarks of cancer and outlines the learning outcomes for understanding how specific genetic mutations drive tumor progression.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and intracellular cascades, such as Wnt/beta-catenin, RTK/Ras/MAPK, and PI3K/Akt, deregulate proliferation and survival signaling.

topics.label: Block in terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how blocks preventing cells from reaching their terminally differentiated state maintain proliferative capacity in leukemias and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through the disruption of p53 regulation and the shifting balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells overcome replicative limits through telomere maintenance, TERT reactivation, and the bypass of p53-mediated stress senescence.

topics.label: Altered cellular metabolism and metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate metabolic alterations in cancer cells, including aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific metabolic profiles, and oncometabolite generation.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch that enables tumors to recruit new blood vessels to overcome hypoxia and meet nutrient demands.

topics.label: Mechanisms and patterns of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the systemic dissemination of cancer cells, including the metastatic cascade, seed-and-soil interactions, and genomic features of metastases.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the key takeaways regarding cancer hallmarks, points students toward recommended literature, and closes the lecture.
